nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.Proves.witness
nodes.doc:
**The witness lemma** (Henkin). Suppose the variable `x` occurs free neither in
the premises `Δ` nor in `∃y φ(y)`. If `Δ ⊢ ∃y φ(y)` and `Δ ∪ {φ(x)}` is
inconsistent, then `Δ` itself is inconsistent. So a fresh variable can always be
consistently declared to be a witness.
nodes.type:
∀ {L : Foundations.Logic.FO.Signature} {Δ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Theory L} {φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula L}
  {x : Nat},
  (∀ (χ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula L), Δ χ → Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Fresh x χ) →
    Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Fresh x φ.ex →
      Δ ⊢₁ φ.ex →
        Δ.insert (φ.inst (Foundations.Logic.FO.Term.var x)) ⊢₁ Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.bot →
          Δ ⊢₁ Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.bot

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.key_identity
nodes.doc: **The key identity.** `Σ_{n ≤ N} χ(n) log n / n = Σ_{d ≤ N} χ(d) Λ(d)/d · Σ_{m ≤ N/d} χ(m)/m`.
nodes.type:
∀ {q : Nat} [inst : NeZero q] (χ : Foundations.NumberTheory.Character (Foundations.Algebra.ZModUnits q)) (N : Nat),
  Foundations.Numbers.gsum
      (fun n =>
        Foundations.NumberTheory.dchar χ n * Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal (Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat n / ↑n))
      (N + 1) =
    Foundations.Numbers.gsum
      (fun d =>
        Foundations.NumberTheory.dchar χ d *
            Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal (Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt d / ↑d) *
          Foundations.NumberTheory.lpart (Foundations.NumberTheory.dchar χ) (N / d + 1))
      (N + 1)

`log(m+1)/((m+1)m) ≤ g(m) − g(m+1)`. It reduces to `(m+1)(log(m+1) − log m) ≤ 2`, which follows

                  W ≤ L * L + (2 + KA') * L + 3 * KA' + 1 →
                    W - W' ≤ Y * (2 * L + KA') →
                      δ₀ * (L * L - c₇ * L) ≤ α * W + C * (W - W') - S →
                        (C * (2 + KA') + 2 * C * Y + δ₀ * c₇ + 2 * K1') * L +

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.omega_nat_iso
nodes.doc:
**ω and Nat are isomorphic structures.** The map `Omega.toNat : ω → Nat` is a
bijection sending `∅` to `0`, set-successor to `+1`, `+ω` to `+`, `*ω` to `*`, and
inclusion to `≤`.

Foundations.Sets.Bijective Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun ∧
  Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun Foundations.Bridges.Omega.zero = 0 ∧
    (∀ (x : Foundations.Bridges.Omega),
        Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun x.succ = Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun x + 1) ∧
      (∀ (x y : Foundations.Bridges.Omega),
          Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun (x.add y) =
            Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun x + Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun y) ∧
        (∀ (x y : Foundations.Bridges.Omega),
            Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun (x.mul y) =
              Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun x * Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun y) ∧
          ∀ (x y : Foundations.Bridges.Omega),
            x.le y ↔ Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun x ≤ Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun y

nodes.name: Foundations.Geometry.Klein.not_euclid
nodes.doc:
**Euclid's axiom fails in the Klein model.** Take the angle at the origin between
the arms through `b = (1/2, 0)` and `c = (0, 1/2)`, and the point `t = (3/5, 3/5)` inside it
(beyond the midpoint `d` of `bc`). Any segment through `t` with endpoints on the two arms
would have endpoints `(σ, 0)`, `(0, ρ)` with `3/5 = (1−λ)σ` and `3/5 = λρ`; since
`σ, ρ < 1` inside the disc this gives `6/5 = (1−λ)σ + λρ < 1`, which is absurd. In
the Euclidean plane the endpoints would simply lie outside the unit circle.
nodes.type:
¬∀ (a b c d t : Foundations.Geometry.Klein.KPt),
    Foundations.Geometry.Klein.KBet a d t →
      Foundations.Geometry.Klein.KBet b d c →
        a ≠ d →
          ∃ x y,
            Foundations.Geometry.Klein.KBet a b x ∧
              Foundations.Geometry.Klein.KBet a c y ∧ Foundations.Geometry.Klein.KBet x t y

nodes.doc:
**Hartogs' theorem.** For every type `α` there is an ordinal `h` that does not
inject into `α`, and it is the least such: an ordinal `o` lies in `h` exactly when
`o` injects into `α`, and every ordinal not injecting into `α` contains or equals `h`.
(The construction makes no choices; see the module docstring for what
`#print axioms` reports.)

∀ (α : Type),
  ∃ h,
    h.IsOrdinal ∧
      (¬∃ f, Function.Injective f) ∧
        (∀ (o : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), o.IsOrdinal → (o ∈ h ↔ ∃ f, Function.Injective f)) ∧
          ∀ (o : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), o.IsOrdinal → (¬∃ f, Function.Injective f) → h = o ∨ h ∈ o

∀ (N : Nat) (g : Nat → Nat → Foundations.Numbers.R),
  Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum

      (fun m => if 1 ≤ m then Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.dsum (fun d => g d (m / d)) m else 0) (N + 1)

  0 ≤ γ →

          1 ≤ M →

              ↑M * (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.harmonic M - (↑M).log - γ) ≤ 1) →
        ∀ {N d : Nat},

                    Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
                      (fun n => if 1 ≤ n then Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.selbergPhi (γ + 1) N (d * n) else 0)

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.Categoricity.exists_rat_sq_between
nodes.doc:
Approximating a square from below by squares of rationals: if `0 < z` and `0 ≤ q < z²`
then some rational `r` with `0 ≤ r < z` has `q < r²`.
nodes.type:
∀ {K : Type} [inst : Lean.Grind.Field K] [inst_1 : LE K] [inst_2 : LT K] [inst_3 : Std.IsLinearOrder K]
  [inst_4 : Std.LawfulOrderLT K] [inst_5 : Lean.Grind.OrderedRing K],
  Foundations.Numbers.OF.Archimedean K →
    ∀ {z : K},
      0 < z →
        ∀ {q : Foundations.Numbers.Q},
          0 ≤ Foundations.Numbers.OF.ofRat q →
            Foundations.Numbers.OF.ofRat q < z * z →
              ∃ r,
                0 < Foundations.Numbers.OF.ofRat r ∧
                  Foundations.Numbers.OF.ofRat r < z ∧
                    Foundations.Numbers.OF.ofRat q < Foundations.Numbers.OF.ofRat r * Foundations.Numbers.OF.ofRat r

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.factorization_unique
nodes.doc:
**Uniqueness of factorisation.** In an integral domain in which every irreducible element
is prime — for instance any principal ideal domain — two factorisations into irreducibles of
associated elements agree up to order and units: if `∏ L = u · ∏ M` with `u` a unit, then for
every `x`, `L` and `M` contain equally many factors associated to `x`.
nodes.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing R],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsDomain R →
    (∀ (p : R), Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible p → Foundations.Algebra.IsPrimeElt p) →
      ∀ (L M : List R) (u : R),
        (∀ (p : R), p ∈ L → Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible p) →
          (∀ (q : R), q ∈ M → Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible q) →
            Foundations.Algebra.IsUnit u →
              Foundations.Algebra.lprod L = u * Foundations.Algebra.lprod M →
                ∀ (x : R), Foundations.Algebra.countAssoc x L = Foundations.Algebra.countAssoc x M

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.dvd_count_of_saturated
nodes.doc:
**The tiling argument.** If a set `P` is a union of left cosets of `H` (i.e. closed under
right multiplication by elements of `H`), then `|H|` divides `|P|`. We peel off one coset
at a time: removing a coset from such a set leaves such a set, with `|H|` fewer elements.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G]
  (H : Foundations.Algebra.Subgroup G) (n : Nat) (P : G → Prop),
  Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.count P = n →
    (∀ (a h : G), P a → h ∈ H → P (a * h)) → (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.count fun x => x ∈ H) ∣ n

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.exists_prime_mod_four_eq_one

      (∀ (χ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula L), χ ∈ A₀ → Foundations.Logic.FO.henkinLimit hΓ₀ A₀ χ) ∧

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.chebyshev_bounds

`⌊m/2⌋ · log 2 ≤ π(m) · log m ≤ m · log 1024`.
So `π(m)` is of order `m / log m`: bounded above and below by constant multiples of it.
nodes.type:
∀ {m : Nat},
  6 ≤ m →
    ↑(m / 2) * Foundations.Numbers.R.log 2 ≤ ↑(Foundations.NumberTheory.primeCount m) * (↑m).log ∧
      ↑(Foundations.NumberTheory.primeCount m) * (↑m).log ≤ ↑m * Foundations.Numbers.R.log 1024

nodes.name: Foundations.Combinatorics.hall
nodes.doc:
**Hall's marriage theorem.** Let `A₀, …, A_{N−1}` be subsets of `{0, …, M−1}` such
that every subfamily `I` has at least `|I|` elements in its union. Then there is a
system of distinct representatives: an injective choice `f(i) ∈ Aᵢ`.
nodes.type:
∀ (N M : Nat) (A : Nat → Nat → Prop),
  (∀ (I : Nat → Prop),
      Foundations.Combinatorics.cnt I N ≤ Foundations.Combinatorics.cnt (Foundations.Combinatorics.union N A I) M) →
    ∃ f, (∀ (i : Nat), i < N → f i < M ∧ A i (f i)) ∧ ∀ (i j : Nat), i < N → j < N → i ≠ j → f i ≠ f j

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.sup_is_union
nodes.doc:
**Dedekind completeness, set-theoretically: the supremum is the union.** If `F` is
a nonempty set of reals (members of ℝ) bounded above by some real `M` (in the order
`⊆`), then the union `⋃F` is again a real, it is an upper bound of `F`, and it lies
below every upper bound. The proof uses nothing but the definition of a cut.
nodes.type:
∀ {F M : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet},
  F ⊆ Foundations.Bridges.RSet →
    (∃ A, A ∈ F) →
      M ∈ Foundations.Bridges.RSet →
        (∀ (A : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), A ∈ F → A ⊆ M) →
          ⋃₀ F ∈ Foundations.Bridges.RSet ∧
            (∀ (A : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), A ∈ F → A ⊆ ⋃₀ F) ∧
              ∀ (M' : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), (∀ (A : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), A ∈ F → A ⊆ M') → ⋃₀ F ⊆ M'

∀ {α : Type} {S : Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.SigmaAlgebra α} (m : Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Measure S)

    (∀ (x : α), 0 ≤ g x) →
      ∀ {φ ψ : List (Foundations.Numbers.R × (α → Prop))},
        Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.IsSimple S φ →
          Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.IsSimple S ψ →
            Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Below φ f →
              Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Below ψ g →
                (Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.BddIntegral m fun x => f x + g x) →
                  Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.sint m φ + Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.sint m ψ ≤
                    Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.lintegral m fun x => f x + g x

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.galois_correspondence
nodes.doc:
**Galois correspondence (the part formalised here).** For a Galois extension `L/K` with
Galois group enumerated as `σ₁, …, σₙ`:
* `[L : Fix(G)] = |G| = [L : K]` and `Fix(G) = K`;
* for every finite subgroup `H` (given as a family `ρ`), `[L : Fix(H)] = |H|` and
  `Aut(L/Fix(H)) = H`.
nodes.type:
∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω →
    ∀ {K L : Foundations.Algebra.Subfield Ω} (hKL : K.le L),
      Foundations.Algebra.IsGalois K L hKL →
        (∀ (x : Ω), (x ∈ Foundations.Algebra.fixedField L fun x => True) → x ∈ K) ∧
          ∀ {m : Nat} (ρ : Fin m → Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut K L),
            (∀ (i j : Fin m), ρ i = ρ j → i = j) →
              (∃ i, ρ i = 1) →
                (∀ (i j : Fin m), ∃ k, ρ k = ρ i * ρ j) →
                  (Foundations.Algebra.famFix ρ).deg L ⋯ = m ∧
                    ∀ (τ : Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut (Foundations.Algebra.famFix ρ) L), ∃ i, (ρ i).toFun = τ.toFun

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.rat_in_sets
nodes.doc:
**The rationals live in the set-theoretic universe.** The comparison map from
Part II's rationals `Q` to the ZF set `ℚ` (classes of pairs `⟪x, k⟫` with `x` in the
ZF set `ℤ` and `k ∈ ω ∖ {∅}`) is a bijection onto the members of `ℚ` preserving
`0`, `1`, addition, negation, multiplication and order.
nodes.type:
(Foundations.Sets.Bijective fun x => ⟨Foundations.Bridges.qToSet x, ⋯⟩) ∧
  Foundations.Bridges.qToSet 0 = Foundations.Bridges.qzero ∧
    Foundations.Bridges.qToSet 1 = Foundations.Bridges.qone ∧
      (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Q),
          Foundations.Bridges.qToSet (x + y) =
            Foundations.Bridges.qadd (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet y)) ∧
        (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.Q),
            Foundations.Bridges.qToSet (-x) = Foundations.Bridges.qneg (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet x)) ∧
          (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Q),
              Foundations.Bridges.qToSet (x * y) =
                Foundations.Bridges.qmul (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet y)) ∧
            ∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Q),
              x ≤ y ↔ Foundations.Bridges.qle (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet y)

nodes.name: Foundations.Probability.FinProb.weak_law_limit
nodes.doc:
**The weak law of large numbers, limit form**: for every `ε > 0` and `δ > 0` there is
`N` such that for all `n ≥ N`, `Pⁿ(|Sₙ/n − μ| ≥ ε) ≤ δ` — the sample mean converges to
the true mean in probability.
nodes.type:

          N ≤ n →

                δ

`Pₙ(a) Pₙ(b) = Pₙ(a + b) + Tₙ(a, b)` with `Pₙ(x) = Σ_{k<n} e x k`.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} [inst : Lean.Grind.Field α] (e : α → Nat → α),
  (∀ (x : α), e x 0 = 1) →
    (∀ (x : α) (n : Nat), (↑n + 1) * e x (n + 1) = x * e x n) →
      (∀ (n : Nat), ↑n + 1 ≠ 0) →
        ∀ (a b : α) (N : Nat),
          Foundations.Numbers.gsum (e a) N * Foundations.Numbers.gsum (e b) N =
            Foundations.Numbers.gsum (e (a + b)) N +
              Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun i => e a i * Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun k => e b (N - i + k)) i) N

**Counting pairs `(d, m)` with `d m ≤ N` in two ways.** If `F(0, m) = F(d, 0) = 0`, then
`Σ_{n ≤ N} Σ_{d ∣ n} F(d, n/d) = Σ_{d ≤ N} Σ_{m ≤ N/d} F(d, m)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} [inst : Lean.Grind.Field α] (F : Nat → Nat → α),
  (∀ (m : Nat), F 0 m = 0) →
    (∀ (d : Nat), F d 0 = 0) →
      ∀ (N : Nat),
        Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun n => Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun d => if d ∣ n then F d (n / d) else 0) (n + 1))
            (N + 1) =
          Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun d => Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun m => F d m) (N / d + 1)) (N + 1)

          (Foundations.Logic.FO.box Foundations.Logic.FO.provPA ψ))) →
  (∀ (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith),
      Foundations.Logic.FO.PA ⊢₁
        (Foundations.Logic.FO.box Foundations.Logic.FO.provPA φ).imp
          (Foundations.Logic.FO.box Foundations.Logic.FO.provPA
            (Foundations.Logic.FO.box Foundations.Logic.FO.provPA φ))) →

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Gentzen.consistency_by_descent
nodes.doc:
**Consistency by ordinal descent** (the abstract form of Gentzen's argument).
Let `D` be a type of objects (e.g. derivations), `Bad` a property of them (e.g. "is
a derivation of the empty sequent"), and `o` an assignment of ordinal notations
below ε₀ in Cantor normal form. If every bad object can be reduced to a bad object of
strictly smaller ordinal, then no object is bad. The proof is transfinite induction
up to ε₀, i.e. the well-foundedness theorem `wellFounded_R`.
nodes.type:
∀ {D : Type} (Bad : D → Prop) (o : D → Foundations.Logic.Ordinals.ON),
  (∀ (d : D), (o d).NF) → (∀ (d : D), Bad d → ∃ d', Bad d' ∧ (o d').lt (o d)) → ∀ (d : D), ¬Bad d

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Sequent.derives_iff_cutFree

from a (possibly infinite) theory `Γ` iff some finite list `L` of premises from `Γ`
gives a *cut-free* sequent derivation of `L ⊢ φ` — which by the subformula property
mentions only subformulas of `L` and `φ`.
nodes.type:
∀ {Γ : Foundations.Logic.Theory} {φ : Foundations.Logic.Formula},
  Γ ⊢ φ ↔ ∃ L, (∀ (ψ : Foundations.Logic.Formula), ψ ∈ L → Γ ψ) ∧ Foundations.Logic.Sequent.CutFree L [φ]

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.artin_dependent
nodes.doc:
**Artin's key lemma.** If `H = {σ₁, …, σₙ}` is a finite group of automorphisms of `L`
(distinct, containing the identity, closed under composition), then any `m > n` elements of `L`
are linearly dependent over `Fix(H)`.

∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω] {K L : Foundations.Algebra.Subfield Ω} {n : Nat}
  (σ : Fin n → Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut K L),
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω →
    (∀ (i j : Fin n), σ i = σ j → i = j) →
      (∃ i, σ i = 1) →
        (∀ (i j : Fin n), ∃ k, σ k = σ i * σ j) →
          ∀ {m : Nat} (a : Fin m → { x // x ∈ L }),
            n < m →
              ∃ c,
                (∃ j, c j ≠ 0) ∧
                  (∀ (j : Fin m), (c j).val ∈ Foundations.Algebra.famFix σ) ∧
                    (Foundations.Algebra.isum fun j => c j * a j) = 0

nodes.name: Foundations.Probability.FinProb.weak_law
nodes.doc:
**The weak law of large numbers** (Bernoulli 1713, in Chebyshev's form). For `n ≥ 1`
independent repetitions and any `ε > 0`,

`Pⁿ(|Sₙ/n − μ| ≥ ε) ≤ σ² / (n ε²)`, where `μ = E[X]`, `σ² = Var X`.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} (P : Foundations.Probability.FinProb α) (X : α → Foundations.Numbers.R) {n : Nat},
  0 < n →
    ∀ {ε : Foundations.Numbers.R},
      0 < ε →
        ((P.pow n).prob fun t =>
            ε ≤ Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.Probability.FinProb.sampleSum X n t / ↑n - P.E X)) ≤
          P.Var X / (↑n * (ε * ε))

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.column_count

**One column of lattice points.** For `1 ≤ x ≤ (p-1)/2`, the number of `y ∈ {1, …, (q-1)/2}`

nodes.type:
∀ {p q : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime q →
      p % 2 = 1 →
        q % 2 = 1 →
          p ≠ q →
            ∀ {x : Nat},
              x < Foundations.Algebra.half p →
                List.countP (fun y => decide (p * (y + 1) < q * (x + 1))) (List.range (Foundations.Algebra.half q)) =
                  q * (x + 1) / p

there is a prime `p ≥ N₀` with `p ≡ a (mod q)`.

      χ ≠ Foundations.NumberTheory.Character.one → Foundations.NumberTheory.Lone χ ≠ 0) →
    ∀ (a : Nat), a.Coprime q → ∀ (N₀ : Nat), ∃ p, N₀ ≤ p ∧ Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p ∧ p % q = a % q

function on judgements, there is a code which on input `a` finds a valid tree whose
root has key `a` (and diverges if there is none).

∀ (step : Nat → Nat → Nat → Bool),
  (Foundations.Logic.Computability.CompB fun n =>
      step (Foundations.Logic.Computability.fst n)
        (Foundations.Logic.Computability.fst (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd n))

              Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval c [a] t →
                Foundations.Logic.Computability.tvalid step t = 1 ∧ key (Foundations.Logic.Computability.troot t) = a) ∧
            ∀ (a : Nat),
              (∃ t,
                  Foundations.Logic.Computability.tvalid step t = 1 ∧
                    key (Foundations.Logic.Computability.troot t) = a) →
                ∃ t, Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval c [a] t

      ∃ χ, ∀ (w : Foundations.Logic.FO.Term L), χ.inst w = Φ fun i => if i = k then w else us i) →
    ∀ {ts ts' : Fin n → Foundations.Logic.FO.Term L},
      (∀ (i : Fin n), Γ ⊢₁ Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.eq (ts i) (ts' i)) → Γ ⊢₁ Φ ts → Γ ⊢₁ Φ ts'

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.godel_second_PA_unconditional
nodes.doc:
**Gödel's second incompleteness theorem for PA.** Unconditionally, PA does not prove
the consistency statement `¬provH(⌜⊥⌝)` for the provability formula `provH`, which defines
PA-provability in the standard model and satisfies (D1)–(D3) provably in PA.

Caveat (Gödel II is intensional, Feferman 1960): `provH` is not the textbook "there is a
PA-derivation of x"; its proofs are modus-ponens/necessitation closures of a Σ₁ listing of
PA's theorems, and PA-provable equivalence of `conF provH` with the canonical Con(PA) is not
established here. `provH` contains no consistency filter, so this is a genuine instance of
the Hilbert–Bernays–Löb form of the theorem, not a Feferman-style artefact.
nodes.type: ¬Foundations.Logic.FO.PA ⊢₁ Foundations.Logic.FO.conF Foundations.Logic.FO.provH

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.good_weight
nodes.doc:
**The combinatorial core of the improvement.** Suppose `|V(n)| ≤ α` for `n ≥ N₀`, and
`m_j` (`j = 0, 1, …`) are left ends of good intervals (`|V| ≤ ε/2` on `[m_j, m_j + ⌊m_j/T⌋]`),
increasing fast enough (`m_{j+1} ≥ m_j + ⌊m_j/T⌋`), with `m_j ≥ Y₀ ≥ N₀`, `m_j ≥ 2T`, and
`64 T² m_j² ≤ N` for `j < J`. Then, with `S = Σ_{k ≤ N} (a(k)/k) |V(⌊N/k⌋)|`,
`8T (α F(N) + C₀ (F(N) − F(N/Y₀)) − S) ≥ J (α − ε/2)(log N − 16 T KA)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {ε α : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  ε ≤ α →
    0 < ε →
      ∀ {N₀ Y₀ T N J : Nat},
        1 ≤ T →
          N₀ ≤ Y₀ →
            1 ≤ Y₀ →
              (∀ (n : Nat), N₀ ≤ n → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vrem n) ≤ α) →
                ∀ (m : Nat → Nat),
                  (∀ (j : Nat), Y₀ ≤ m j) →
                    (∀ (j : Nat), 2 * T ≤ m j) →
                      (∀ (j : Nat), m j + m j / T ≤ m (j + 1)) →
                        (∀ (j n : Nat),
                            m j ≤ n →
                              n ≤ m j + m j / T →
                                Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vrem n) ≤ ε / 2) →
                          (∀ (j : Nat), j < J → 64 * (T * T) * (m j * m j) ≤ N) →
                            ↑J * ((α - ε / 2) * ((↑N).log - 16 * ↑T * Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.KA)) ≤
                              8 * ↑T *
                                (α * Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.wsum N +
                                    Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.C0 *
                                      (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.wsum N -
                                        Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.wsum (N / Y₀)) -
                                  Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
                                    (fun k =>
                                      Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.selA k * (1 / ↑k) *
                                        Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vrem (N / k)))
                                    (N + 1))

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.uniform_square
nodes.doc:
**Uniform continuity on the square.** (A Lebesgue-number lemma for `[0, 1]²`.) For jointly
continuous `H` and `ε > 0` there is `δ > 0` such that `H(s, u)` and `H(s, v)` are `ε`-close
whenever `s, u, v ∈ [0, 1]` and `|u − v| < δ`.
nodes.type:
∀ {X : Type} [inst : Foundations.Topology.MetricSpace X] {H : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R → X},
  Foundations.Topology.Cont2 H →
    ∀ {ε : Foundations.Numbers.R},
      0 < ε →
        ∃ δ,
          0 < δ ∧
            ∀ (s u v : Foundations.Numbers.R),
              0 ≤ s →
                s ≤ 1 →
                  0 ≤ u →
                    u ≤ 1 →
                      0 ≤ v →
                        v ≤ 1 → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (u - v) < δ → Foundations.Topology.dist (H s u) (H s v) < ε

            Foundations.Types.STLC.RED (A.sum B) t →
              (∀ (a : Foundations.Types.STLC.Term),
                  Foundations.Types.STLC.RED A a → Foundations.Types.STLC.RED C (Foundations.Types.STLC.inst u₁ a)) →
                (∀ (b : Foundations.Types.STLC.Term),

                  Foundations.Types.STLC.RED C (t.case u₁ u₂)

  Foundations.Topology.Cont2 H →

      (∀ (s : Foundations.Numbers.R), 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 → H s 1 = H s 0) →
        Foundations.Topology.degree (H 0) = Foundations.Topology.degree (H 1)

            S U →
              S V →

          Foundations.Sets.Countable { U // S U }

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.int_in_sets
nodes.doc:
**The integers live in the set-theoretic universe.** The comparison map from
Part II's integers `Z` to the ZF set `ℤ` of equivalence classes of pairs in `ω × ω`
is a bijection onto the members of `ℤ` that preserves `0`, `1`, addition, negation,
multiplication and order — all of which are defined on the set side by the ZF
axioms alone (pairs, products, separation, power set, and `+ω`, `*ω`).
nodes.type:
(Foundations.Sets.Bijective fun x => ⟨Foundations.Bridges.zToSet x, ⋯⟩) ∧
  Foundations.Bridges.zToSet 0 = Foundations.Bridges.zzero ∧
    Foundations.Bridges.zToSet 1 = Foundations.Bridges.zone ∧
      (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
          Foundations.Bridges.zToSet (x + y) =
            Foundations.Bridges.zadd (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet y)) ∧
        (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
            Foundations.Bridges.zToSet (-x) = Foundations.Bridges.zneg (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet x)) ∧
          (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
              Foundations.Bridges.zToSet (x * y) =
                Foundations.Bridges.zmul (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet y)) ∧
            ∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
              x ≤ y ↔ Foundations.Bridges.zle (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet y)

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.banach_fixed_point
nodes.doc:
**Banach's fixed-point theorem.** On a complete metric space, a contraction `f`
(`d(f x, f y) ≤ q d(x, y)` with `0 ≤ q < 1`) has a unique fixed point, and the orbit of every
starting point converges to it.
nodes.type:
∀ {X : Type} [inst : Foundations.Topology.MetricSpace X],
  Foundations.Topology.Complete X →
    ∀ {f : X → X} {q : Foundations.Numbers.R},
      0 ≤ q →
        q < 1 →
          (∀ (x y : X), Foundations.Topology.dist (f x) (f y) ≤ q * Foundations.Topology.dist x y) →
            ∀ (x₀ : X),
              ∃ x,
                f x = x ∧
                  Foundations.Topology.Converges (Foundations.Topology.orbit f x₀) x ∧ ∀ (y : X), f y = y → y = x

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.le_of_deg_eq
nodes.doc:
**Equal degrees force equality.** If `K ⊆ F ⊆ L` and `[L : F] = [L : K]` (both finite), then
`F = K`. (Proof: a basis of `L` over `F` is independent over `K` and has the right size, hence
is a basis over `K`; comparing coordinates of `f · b` in the two bases shows `f ∈ K`.)
nodes.type:
∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω →
    ∀ {K F L : Foundations.Algebra.Subfield Ω},
      K.le F →
        ∀ (hFL : F.le L) (hKL : K.le L), K.FiniteExt L hKL → F.FiniteExt L hFL → F.deg L hFL = K.deg L hKL → F.le K

nodes.name: Foundations.Categories.Lambek.semSub_lift_aux
nodes.doc:
The interpretation of a lifted substitution is `⟦σ⟧ × 𝟙`, provided weakening is
interpreted by the first projection.
nodes.type:
∀ {C : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Categories.Category C] [inst_1 : Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed C]
  (ι : Nat → C) {Δ Γ : List Foundations.Categories.Lambek.FTy} {B : Foundations.Categories.Lambek.FTy}
  (σ : Foundations.Categories.Lambek.Sub Γ Δ) (σ' : Foundations.Categories.Lambek.Sub (B :: Γ) (B :: Δ)),
  Foundations.Categories.Lambek.semTm ι (σ' Foundations.Categories.Lambek.Mem.here) =
      Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.snd →
    (∀ {A : Foundations.Categories.Lambek.FTy} (v : Foundations.Categories.Lambek.Mem A Γ),
        Foundations.Categories.Lambek.semTm ι (σ' v.there) =
          Foundations.Categories.Category.comp Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.fst
            (Foundations.Categories.Lambek.semTm ι (σ v))) →
      (Foundations.Categories.Lambek.semSub ι fun {A} => σ') =
        Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.pair
          (Foundations.Categories.Category.comp Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.fst
            (Foundations.Categories.Lambek.semSub ι fun {A} => σ))
          Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.snd

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.fixedField_injective

nodes.name: Foundations.Categories.Adjunction.preservesLimit
nodes.doc:
**RAPL: right adjoints preserve limits.** If `G` has a left adjoint `F` and `c` is a
limit of a diagram `K : J ⥤ D`, then `G c` is a limit of `K ⋙ G`. The proof transposes
a cone `W ⟶ G (K j)` across the adjunction to a cone `F W ⟶ K j`, factors that through
`c`, and transposes back.
nodes.type:
{J : Type u₁} →
  [inst : Foundations.Categories.Category J] →
    {C : Type u} →
      [inst_1 : Foundations.Categories.Category C] →
        {D : Type u₂} →
          [inst_2 : Foundations.Categories.Category D] →
            {F : Foundations.Categories.Functor C D} →
              {G : Foundations.Categories.Functor D C} →
                Foundations.Categories.Adjunction F G →
                  {K : Foundations.Categories.Functor J D} →
                    {c : Foundations.Categories.Cone K} →
                      Foundations.Categories.IsLimit c → Foundations.Categories.IsLimit (c.map G)

  Foundations.Algebra.KummerChain m →
    ∀ {p : Nat},

          Foundations.Algebra.rpow ζ p = 1 →

                (∀ (y : Foundations.Numbers.C),
                    y ∈ ys → Foundations.Algebra.rpow y p ∈ Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc m) →

nodes.doc:

`−3 ≤ Σ_{p ≤ N} log p / p − log N ≤ log 1024`, i.e. `Σ_{p ≤ N} log p / p = log N + O(1)`.

∀ {N : Nat},
  1 ≤ N →
    -3 ≤
        Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum (fun p => if Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p then (↑p).log * (1 / ↑p) else 0)

          (↑N).log ∧
      Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum (fun p => if Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p then (↑p).log * (1 / ↑p) else 0)
            (N + 1) -
          (↑N).log ≤
        Foundations.Numbers.R.log 1024

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Computability.tvalid_iff
nodes.doc:
Unfolding validity: a tree is valid iff its root follows by a rule from the roots of
its subtrees, and all subtrees are smaller and valid.
nodes.type:
∀ (step : Nat → Nat → Nat → Bool) (t : Nat),
  Foundations.Logic.Computability.tvalid step t = 1 ↔
    step (Foundations.Logic.Computability.troot t)
          (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd (Foundations.Logic.Computability.fst t))
          (Foundations.Logic.Computability.fst (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) =
        true ∧
      Foundations.Logic.Computability.llen
            (Foundations.Logic.Computability.fst (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) =
          Foundations.Logic.Computability.llen
            (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) ∧
        ∀ (i : Nat),
          i <
              Foundations.Logic.Computability.llen
                (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) →
            Foundations.Logic.Computability.lnth
                  (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) i <
                t ∧
              Foundations.Logic.Computability.tvalid step
                    (Foundations.Logic.Computability.lnth
                      (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) i) =
                  1 ∧
                Foundations.Logic.Computability.troot
                    (Foundations.Logic.Computability.lnth
                      (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) i) =
                  Foundations.Logic.Computability.lnth
                    (Foundations.Logic.Computability.fst (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) i

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.R.ordered_field
nodes.doc:
**ℝ is an ordered field.** The field laws hold, every non-zero real has an inverse, and `≤`
is a linear order compatible with addition and with multiplication by positive reals.
nodes.type:
(∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.R), x + y + z = x + (y + z)) ∧
  (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.R), x + y = y + x) ∧
    (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), x + 0 = x) ∧
      (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), -x + x = 0) ∧
        (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.R), x * y * z = x * (y * z)) ∧
          (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.R), x * y = y * x) ∧
            (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), x * 1 = x) ∧
              (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.R), x * (y + z) = x * y + x * z) ∧
                0 ≠ 1 ∧
                  (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), x ≠ 0 → x * x⁻¹ = 1) ∧
                    (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.R), x ≤ y → y ≤ z → x ≤ z) ∧
                      (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.R), x ≤ y → y ≤ x → x = y) ∧
                        (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.R), x ≤ y ∨ y ≤ x) ∧
                          (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.R), x ≤ y → x + z ≤ y + z) ∧
                            ∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.R), x < y → 0 < z → z * x < z * y

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.peel_blocks
nodes.doc:
**Peeling.** If `g ≥ 0` on `[0, N]` and the ranges `(lo_j, hi_j]` are disjoint and decreasing
(`hi_{j+1} ≤ lo_j ≤ hi_j`, `hi_0 ≤ N`), then
`Σ_{j < J} Σ_{lo_j < k ≤ hi_j} g(k) ≤ Σ_{k ≤ N} g(k)` (block sums written as differences of
partial sums).
nodes.type:
∀ (g : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.R) {N : Nat},
  (∀ (k : Nat), k ≤ N → 0 ≤ g k) →
    ∀ (lo hi : Nat → Nat),
      (∀ (j : Nat), lo j ≤ hi j) →
        (∀ (j : Nat), hi (j + 1) ≤ lo j) →
          hi 0 ≤ N →
            ∀ (J : Nat),
              Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
                  (fun j => Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum g (hi j + 1) - Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum g (lo j + 1)) J ≤
                Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum g (N + 1)

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.Path.homotopic_of_reparam
nodes.doc:
**Reparametrisation lemma.** If `P = g ∘ φ` and `Q = g ∘ ψ` on `[0, 1]` for one continuous
`g` and continuous reparametrisations `φ, ψ` with the same values at `0` and `1`, then `P` and `Q`
are homotopic: slide linearly from `φ` to `ψ`.
nodes.type:
∀ {X : Type} [inst : Foundations.Topology.MetricSpace X] {x y : X} {g : Foundations.Numbers.R → X},
  Foundations.Topology.Continuous g →
    ∀ {φ ψ : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R},
      Foundations.Topology.Continuous φ →
        Foundations.Topology.Continuous ψ →
          φ 0 = ψ 0 →
            φ 1 = ψ 1 →
              ∀ (P Q : Foundations.Topology.Path x y),
                (∀ (t : Foundations.Numbers.R), 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → P.toFun t = g (φ t)) →
                  (∀ (t : Foundations.Numbers.R), 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → Q.toFun t = g (ψ t)) → P.Homotopic Q

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Computability.incompleteness
nodes.doc:
**Abstract incompleteness theorem** (computational form of Gödel's first
incompleteness theorem; *abstract* — see the module docstring for exactly which
hypotheses remain to be discharged for a concrete system such as PA).

Let `Provable c x` mean "the formal system proves that code `c` does not halt on
input `x`". Suppose the system is
* **sound** for such statements: it proves only true ones; and
* **computably enumerable**: some code `q` halts on `(⌜c⌝, x)` exactly when
  `Provable c x`.

Then the system is **incomplete**: there is an explicit code `c` and input `x` such
that `c` does not halt on `x`, yet this is not provable. Namely `c = godelCode q` and
`x = ⌜c⌝` — the statement "I am not provable", in computational dress.
nodes.type:
∀ (Provable : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code → Nat → Prop),
  (∀ (c : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code) (x : Nat),
      Provable c x → ¬Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts c [x]) →
    ∀ {q : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code},
      (∀ (c : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code) (x : Nat),
          Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts q [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c, x] ↔ Provable c x) →
        ¬Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts (Foundations.Logic.Computability.godelCode q)
              [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode (Foundations.Logic.Computability.godelCode q)] ∧
          ¬Provable (Foundations.Logic.Computability.godelCode q)
              (Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode (Foundations.Logic.Computability.godelCode q))

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.Z.bridge_int
nodes.doc:
**Bridge theorem (ℤ).** The equivalence `Z ≃ Int` preserves `0`, `1`, addition, negation,
multiplication and order. So the integers built from pairs of naturals are the same structure as
Lean's `Int`, and we use `Int` from now on.
nodes.type:
Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun 0 = 0 ∧
  Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun 1 = 1 ∧
    (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
        Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun (x + y) =
          Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun x + Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun y) ∧
      (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
          Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun (-x) = -Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun x) ∧
        (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
            Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun (x * y) =
              Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun x * Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun y) ∧

nodes.name: Foundations.Probability.FinProb.bayes_total

**Bayes' theorem with the law of total probability** in the denominator:
`P(B | A) = P(A | B) P(B) / (P(A | B) P(B) + P(A | Bᶜ) P(Bᶜ))`.

∀ {α : Type} (P : Foundations.Probability.FinProb α) {A B : Foundations.Probability.FinProb.Event α},
  P.prob B ≠ 0 →
    (P.prob fun x => ¬B x) ≠ 0 →
      P.cond B A = P.cond A B * P.prob B / (P.cond A B * P.prob B + (P.cond A fun x => ¬B x) * P.prob fun x => ¬B x)

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.mobius_identity
nodes.doc: **The Möbius identity.** `log N + S_χ(N) = Σ_{d ≤ N} χ(d) μ(d) (log N − log d)/d · Σ_{m ≤ N/d} χ(m)/m`.
nodes.type:
∀ {q : Nat} [inst : NeZero q] (χ : Foundations.NumberTheory.Character (Foundations.Algebra.ZModUnits q)) (N : Nat),
  Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal (Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat N) + Foundations.NumberTheory.chebSum χ N =
    Foundations.Numbers.gsum
      (fun d =>
        Foundations.NumberTheory.dchar χ d *
            Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal
              (Foundations.NumberTheory.mobius d * (Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat N - Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat d) /
                ↑d) *
          Foundations.NumberTheory.lpart (Foundations.NumberTheory.dchar χ) (N / d + 1))
      (N + 1)

∀ {N s : Nat},
  1 ≤ N →

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.prime_power_sum_le

**Higher prime powers contribute boundedly.**
`Σ_{p ≤ N} Σ_{k ≤ N} [p prime, k ≥ 2, pᵏ ≤ N] log p / pᵏ ≤ 4`.

∀ (N : Nat),
  Foundations.Numbers.gsum
      (fun p =>
        Foundations.Numbers.gsum
          (fun k =>
            if Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p ∧ 2 ≤ k ∧ p ^ k ≤ N then Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat p / ↑(p ^ k)
            else 0)
          (N + 1))
      (N + 1) ≤
    4

nodes.name: Foundations.Sets.ZFSet.recursion_theorem
nodes.doc:
**Dedekind's recursion theorem.** Let `a ∈ A` and let `g` map `A` into `A`.
Then there is exactly one function `F` from `ω` to `A` (a set of pairs) with
`F(∅) = a` and `F(succ n) = g(F(n))` for all `n ∈ ω`.
nodes.type:
∀ {A a : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet},
  a ∈ A →
    ∀ (g : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet → Foundations.Sets.ZFSet),
      (∀ (x : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), x ∈ A → g x ∈ A) →
        ∃ F,
          F.IsFunction ω A ∧
            F.app ∅ = a ∧
              (∀ (n : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), n ∈ ω → F.app n.succ = g (F.app n)) ∧
                ∀ (G : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet),
                  G.IsFunction ω A →
                    G.app ∅ = a → (∀ (n : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), n ∈ ω → G.app n.succ = g (G.app n)) → G = F

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.Ascoli.arzela_ascoli
nodes.doc:
**Arzelà–Ascoli theorem.** A uniformly bounded, equicontinuous sequence of functions on
`[a, b]` has a subsequence converging uniformly on `[a, b]`.
nodes.type:
∀ {fs : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R} {a b : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  a ≤ b →
    (∃ B, ∀ (n : Nat) (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), a ≤ x → x ≤ b → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (fs n x) ≤ B) →
      (∀ (ε : Foundations.Numbers.R),
          0 < ε →
            ∃ δ,
              0 < δ ∧
                ∀ (n : Nat) (x y : Foundations.Numbers.R),
                  a ≤ x →
                    x ≤ b →
                      a ≤ y →
                        y ≤ b →
                          Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (x - y) < δ → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (fs n x - fs n y) < ε) →
        ∃ φ,
          (∀ (k : Nat), φ k < φ (k + 1)) ∧ ∃ g, Foundations.Topology.UnifOn (fun k => fs (φ k)) g fun x => a ≤ x ∧ x ≤ b

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.levels_spec
nodes.doc: The properties of the levels.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} {S : Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.SigmaAlgebra α} {f : α → Foundations.Numbers.R},
  Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Measurable S f →
    (∀ (x : α), 0 ≤ f x) →
      ∀ {δ : Foundations.Numbers.R},
        0 < δ →
          ∀ (K : Nat),
            (∀ (l : Foundations.Numbers.R × Foundations.Numbers.R × (α → Prop)),
                l ∈ Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.levels f δ K → S.M l.snd.snd) ∧
              Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.DisjOn (fun l => l.snd.snd)
                  (Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.levels f δ K) ∧
                (∀ (x : α),
                    Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.UnionOf (fun l => l.snd.snd)
                      (Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.levels f δ K) x) ∧
                  ∀ (l : Foundations.Numbers.R × Foundations.Numbers.R × (α → Prop)),
                    l ∈ Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.levels f δ K →
                      0 ≤ l.fst ∧
                        l.snd.fst = l.fst + δ ∧
                          ∀ (x : α), l.snd.snd x → l.fst ≤ f x ∧ (f x < l.snd.fst ∨ ↑K * δ ≤ l.fst)

nodes.name: Foundations.Geometry.Klein.determination
nodes.doc:
**The determination lemma.** If `1 = λp + μq`, `p = λ + μγ`, `q = λγ + μ` with
`λ ≥ 0`, `μ > 0`, `γ > 1`, and the same holds for `λ', μ', γ'` with the *same* `p, q`,
then `λ = λ'` and `μ = μ'`.
nodes.type:
∀ {p q l m g l' m' g' : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  0 ≤ l →
    0 < m →
      1 < g →
        0 ≤ l' →
          0 < m' →
            1 < g' →
              1 = l * p + m * q →
                p = l + m * g →
                  q = l * g + m → 1 = l' * p + m' * q → p = l' + m' * g' → q = l' * g' + m' → l = l' ∧ m = m'

    (∀ (a b : Foundations.Numbers.N),

          Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun a + Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun b) ∧
      (∀ (a b : Foundations.Numbers.N),
          Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun (a * b) =
            Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun a * Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun b) ∧

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.R.abs_rsum_sub_rsum_le
nodes.doc:
**Comparison lemma.** If `|f s − f s'| ≤ ε` whenever `s, s' ∈ [A, B]` are within `2δ`, then
the Riemann sums over any two `δ`-fine partitions of `[a, b]` differ by at most `ε (b − a)`.
Proof: walk along both partitions simultaneously, each time cutting off the shorter of the two
first pieces.
nodes.type:
∀ {f : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R} {A B δ ε : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  (∀ (s s' : Foundations.Numbers.R),
      A ≤ s →
        s ≤ B →
          A ≤ s' → s' ≤ B → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (s - s') < 2 * δ → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (f s - f s') ≤ ε) →
    ∀ (n : Nat) (a b : Foundations.Numbers.R) (P Q : List (Foundations.Numbers.R × Foundations.Numbers.R)),
      P.length + Q.length ≤ n →
        A.Fine B δ a P b →
          A.Fine B δ a Q b →

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.dedekind
nodes.doc:
**Dedekind's lemma on the independence of characters.** Pairwise distinct maps
`χ₁, …, χₙ : F → F` into a field that are multiplicative (`χ(xy) = χ(x)χ(y)`, `χ(1) = 1`) are
linearly independent over `F`: if `∑ cᵢ χᵢ(x) = 0` for all `x`, then every `cᵢ = 0`.
nodes.type:
∀ {F : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing F],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField F →
    ∀ (n : Nat) (χ : Fin n → F → F),
      (∀ (i : Fin n) (x y : F), χ i (x * y) = χ i x * χ i y) →
        (∀ (i : Fin n), χ i 1 = 1) →
          (∀ (i j : Fin n), χ i = χ j → i = j) →
            ∀ (c : Fin n → F), (∀ (x : F), (Foundations.Algebra.isum fun i => c i * χ i x) = 0) → ∀ (i : Fin n), c i = 0

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.unique_factorization

**Unique factorisation in `F[x]`.** Over a field, every non-zero non-unit polynomial is a
product of irreducible polynomials, uniquely up to order and constant factors.
nodes.type:
∀ {F : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing F],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField F →
    ∀ (p : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial F),
      p ≠ 0 →
        ¬Foundations.Algebra.IsUnit p →
          (∃ L,
              (∀ (q : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial F), q ∈ L → Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible q) ∧
                Foundations.Algebra.lprod L = p) ∧
            ∀ (L M : List (Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial F)),
              (∀ (q : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial F), q ∈ L → Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible q) →
                (∀ (q : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial F), q ∈ M → Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible q) →
                  Foundations.Algebra.lprod L = p →
                    Foundations.Algebra.lprod M = p →
                      ∀ (x : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial F),
                        Foundations.Algebra.countAssoc x L = Foundations.Algebra.countAssoc x M

      ∃ F, Foundations.Bridges.El.map F = f) ∧
    (¬∃ X, Nonempty (Foundations.Categories.Iso (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj X) Foundations.Sets.ZFSet)) ∧
      Nonempty (Foundations.Categories.IsTerminal (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj Foundations.Bridges.zfOne)) ∧
        (∀ (X Y : Foundations.Bridges.ZFCat),
            Nonempty
              (Foundations.Categories.IsProduct (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj X) (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj Y)
                (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj (Foundations.Bridges.zfProd X Y))
                (Foundations.Bridges.El.map (Foundations.Bridges.zfFst X Y))
                (Foundations.Bridges.El.map (Foundations.Bridges.zfSnd X Y)))) ∧
          Nonempty

  Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun n => Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt n * g n) (N + 1) =

        Foundations.Numbers.gsum

            if Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p ∧ 1 ≤ k ∧ p ^ k ≤ N then Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat p * g (p ^ k)
            else 0)

      (N + 1)

A **monad** on `C`: an endofunctor `T` with unit `η_X : X ⟶ T X` and multiplication
`μ_X : T (T X) ⟶ T X`, both natural, such that `μ` is associative and `η` is a two-sided
unit for it.
nodes.type: (C : Type u) → [Foundations.Categories.Category C] → Type (max u v)

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.Arith.gcd_succ
nodes.doc: Defining equation of Euclid's algorithm: `gcd a b = gcd b (a mod b)` for `b > 0`.

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.dist_orbit_add
nodes.doc: Far orbit points: `d(xₙ₊ₖ, xₙ) ≤ qⁿ d(x₁, x₀) (1 − qᵏ)/(1 − q)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {X : Type} [inst : Foundations.Topology.MetricSpace X] {f : X → X} {q : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  0 ≤ q →
    q < 1 →
      (∀ (x y : X), Foundations.Topology.dist (f x) (f y) ≤ q * Foundations.Topology.dist x y) →
        ∀ (x₀ : X) (n k : Nat),
          Foundations.Topology.dist (Foundations.Topology.orbit f x₀ (n + k)) (Foundations.Topology.orbit f x₀ n) ≤
            q ^ n * Foundations.Topology.dist (Foundations.Topology.orbit f x₀ 1) x₀ * ((1 - q ^ k) / (1 - q))

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.lpart
nodes.doc: The partial sums `Σ_{n<N} a(n)/n` of the `L`-series at `s = 1`.
nodes.type: (Nat → Foundations.Numbers.C) → Nat → Foundations.Numbers.C

nodes.name: Foundations.Geometry.rat_not_continuous
nodes.doc:
**Continuity fails in `ℚ²`.** The points `(x, 0)` with `x ≥ 0`, `x² < 2` all
precede, as seen from the origin, the points `(y, 0)` with `y ≥ 0`, `y² > 2`; but no
rational point lies between the two families — the gap is at `√2`.
nodes.type:
¬∀ (φ ψ : Foundations.Geometry.Pt Foundations.Numbers.Q → Prop),
    (∃ a, ∀ (x y : Foundations.Geometry.Pt Foundations.Numbers.Q), φ x → ψ y → a.Bet x y) →
      ∃ b, ∀ (x y : Foundations.Geometry.Pt Foundations.Numbers.Q), φ x → ψ y → x.Bet b y

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.liftRel
nodes.doc: A relation on representatives, lifted to classes: some representatives are related.
nodes.type: (Foundations.Sets.ZFSet → Foundations.Sets.ZFSet → Prop) → Foundations.Sets.ZFSet → Foundations.Sets.ZFSet → Prop

nodes.name: Foundations.Types.Lambda.subst_subst
nodes.doc: **Substitutions compose**: substituting `σ` then `τ` is substituting `τ ∘ σ`.
nodes.type:
∀ (t : Foundations.Types.Lambda.Term) (τ σ : Nat → Foundations.Types.Lambda.Term),

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.C.exp_add

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.Cut.mul

nodes.type: Foundations.Numbers.Cut → Foundations.Numbers.Cut → Foundations.Numbers.Cut

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.cabs_lnat_add_chebSum_le
nodes.doc: **If `L(1, χ) = 0` then `S_χ(N) = −log N + O(1)`**: precisely `|log N + S_χ(N)| ≤ 2q`.
nodes.type:
∀ {q : Nat} [inst : NeZero q] (χ : Foundations.NumberTheory.Character (Foundations.Algebra.ZModUnits q)),
  χ ≠ Foundations.NumberTheory.Character.one →
    Foundations.NumberTheory.Lone χ = 0 →
      ∀ {N : Nat},
        0 < N →
          (Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal (Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat N) + Foundations.NumberTheory.chebSum χ N).cabs ≤
            2 * ↑q

substitution for the bound variable.
nodes.type:
∀ {A B : Foundations.Types.STLC.Ty} {s : Foundations.Types.STLC.Term},
  (∀ (u : Foundations.Types.STLC.Term),
      Foundations.Types.STLC.RED A u → Foundations.Types.STLC.RED B (Foundations.Types.STLC.inst s u)) →
    Foundations.Types.STLC.RED (A.arr B) s.lam

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.brouwer_one_dim
nodes.doc:
**Brouwer's fixed-point theorem, dimension 1.** Every `f` continuous at every point of `[0, 1]`
and mapping `[0, 1]` into itself has a fixed point.
nodes.type:
∀ {f : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R},
  (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), 0 ≤ x → x ≤ 1 → Foundations.Numbers.R.ContinuousAt f x) →
    (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), 0 ≤ x → x ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ 1) → ∃ x, 0 ≤ x ∧ x ≤ 1 ∧ f x = x

nodes.name: Foundations.Probability.FinProb.Var_sumN
nodes.doc:
**Bienaymé's identity**: the variance of a sum of pairwise uncorrelated random
variables is the sum of their variances.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} (P : Foundations.Probability.FinProb α) (n : Nat) (X : Nat → α → Foundations.Numbers.R),
  (∀ (i j : Nat), i < j → j < n → P.Uncorr (X i) (X j)) →
    (P.Var fun x => Foundations.Probability.FinProb.sumN n fun i => X i x) =
      Foundations.Probability.FinProb.sumN n fun i => P.Var (X i)

nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} {S : Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.SigmaAlgebra α} (m : Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Measure S)
  {f g : α → Foundations.Numbers.R},
  Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Measurable S f →
    Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.LIntegrable m g →
      (∀ (x : α), Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (f x) ≤ g x) → Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Integrable m f

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.Outer.psum_remove
nodes.doc: Removing the index `j` from the selection.
nodes.type:
∀ (len : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.R) {P : Nat → Prop} {j N : Nat},
  j < N →
    P j →
      Foundations.Topology.Outer.psum len P N = Foundations.Topology.Outer.psum len (fun k => P k ∧ k ≠ j) N + len j ∧
        Foundations.Topology.Outer.pcnt P N = Foundations.Topology.Outer.pcnt (fun k => P k ∧ k ≠ j) N + 1

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.psi_le_primeCount_mul_log

nodes.type: ∀ {N : Nat}, 1 ≤ N → Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.psi N ≤ ↑(Foundations.NumberTheory.primeCount N) * (↑N).log

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Computability.halting_undecidable
nodes.doc:
**Undecidability of the halting problem** (Turing 1936). There is no code `h`
that is total on (Gödel numbers of codes, inputs) and outputs `1` when `c` halts on
`x` and `0` when it does not.
nodes.type:
¬∃ h,
    ∀ (c : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code) (x : Nat),
      (Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval h [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c, x] 0 ∨
          Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval h [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c, x] 1) ∧
        (Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval h [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c, x] 1 ↔
          Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts c [x])

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.R.exists_sqrt_two

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.selberg_symmetry
nodes.doc:
**Selberg's symmetry formula.** For every `N ≥ 1`,
`|ψ(N) log N + Σ_{n ≤ N} Λ(n) ψ(⌊N/n⌋) − 2N log N| ≤ (30 + 3 log 1024) · N`,
i.e. `ψ(x) log x + Σ_{n ≤ x} Λ(n) ψ(x/n) = 2x log x + O(x)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {N : Nat},
  1 ≤ N →
    Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs
        (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.psi N * (↑N).log +
            Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
              (fun n => Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vonMangoldt n * Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.psi (N / n)) (N + 1) -
          2 * ↑N * (↑N).log) ≤
      (30 + 3 * Foundations.Numbers.R.log 1024) * ↑N

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.good_interval
nodes.doc:
**Good intervals.** For every `ε > 0` there are `K, T ≥ 1` and `y₀` such that for every
`y ≥ y₀` some `m ∈ (y, Ky]` has `|V(n)| ≤ ε/2` for all `n ∈ [m, m + ⌊m/T⌋]`.
nodes.type:
∀ {ε : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  0 < ε →
    ∃ K T y₀,
      1 ≤ K ∧
        1 ≤ T ∧
          ∀ (y : Nat),
            y₀ ≤ y →
              ∃ m,
                y < m ∧
                  m ≤ K * y ∧
                    ∀ (n : Nat),
                      m ≤ n → n ≤ m + m / T → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vrem n) ≤ ε / 2

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.C.exists_min_on_square

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.abel_bound
nodes.doc:
**Abel's summation by parts.** If `|Σ_{n<N} a(n)| ≤ B` for all `N`, and `b ≥ 0` is
non-increasing from `M` on, then `|Σ_{M ≤ n < K} a(n) b(n)| ≤ 2 B b(M)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {a : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.C} {B : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  (∀ (N : Nat), (Foundations.Numbers.gsum a N).cabs ≤ B) →
    ∀ {b : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.R} {M : Nat},
      (∀ (n : Nat), M ≤ n → b (n + 1) ≤ b n) →
        (∀ (n : Nat), M ≤ n → 0 ≤ b n) →
          ∀ (K : Nat),
            M ≤ K →
              (Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun n => a n * Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal (b n)) K -
                    Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun n => a n * Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal (b n)) M).cabs ≤
                2 * B * b M

nodes.name: Foundations.Forcing.ccc_iSup_countable
nodes.doc:
**Every supremum in a ccc algebra is a countable supremum.** If `B` is ccc, then for every
family `(bᵢ)_{i ∈ ι}` there is a countable subfamily with the same supremum.

Proof: by Zorn's lemma take a maximal family `M` of pairwise disjoint non-zero elements, each
below some `bᵢ`; it is countable by ccc. Choosing such an `i` for each member of `M` gives a
countable subfamily. If its supremum `T` were below `⨆ᵢ bᵢ` and different from it, some
`bᵢ ⊓ Tᶜ` would be non-zero and could be added to `M`.

This is the algebraic core of the standard proof that ccc forcing preserves cardinals: a
name for a function from `ω` into a ground-model set has, at each argument, only countably
many possible values. That set-theoretic consequence is **not** formalised here.
nodes.type:
∀ {B : Type} [inst : Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra B],
  Foundations.Forcing.IsCCC B →
    ∀ {ι : Type} (b : ι → B),
      ∃ J j,
        Foundations.Sets.Countable J ∧ Foundations.Forcing.CBA.iSup b = Foundations.Forcing.CBA.iSup fun k => b (j k)

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.mem_of_ortho
nodes.doc:
**Every character occurs in an orthogonal family.** If `L` is a non-empty list of characters
with `Σ_{ψ ∈ L} ψ(x) = |L| · [x = 1]`, then every character `χ` belongs to `L`: otherwise each
`ψ · χ̄` would be a non-trivial character, so `Σ_x Σ_ψ ψ(x) χ(x⁻¹) = 0`, while summing in the
other order gives `|L|`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommGroup G] [Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G]
  {L : List (G → Foundations.Numbers.C)},
  L ≠ [] →
    (∀ (ψ : G → Foundations.Numbers.C), ψ ∈ L → Foundations.NumberTheory.IsChar ψ) →
      (∀ (x : G), (Foundations.NumberTheory.lsum L fun ψ => ψ x) = if x = 1 then ↑L.length else 0) →
        ∀ {χ : G → Foundations.Numbers.C}, Foundations.NumberTheory.IsChar χ → χ ∈ L

      ∀ (m n : Nat), Foundations.Sets.ZFSet.vn (m * n) = Foundations.Sets.ZFSet.vn m *ω Foundations.Sets.ZFSet.vn n

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.lintegral_add
nodes.doc:

nodes.name: Foundations.Categories.lawvere_fixed_point
nodes.doc:
**Lawvere's fixed-point theorem.** Let `A × A` be a product (projections `p₁, p₂`)
and `φ : A × A ⟶ B` be point-surjective with respect to `T`-points: for every
`g : A ⟶ B` there is `a : T ⟶ A` with `φ ∘ ⟨a, x⟩ = g ∘ x` for all `x : T ⟶ A`. Then every
`t : B ⟶ B` has a fixed `T`-point `b : T ⟶ B`, `b ≫ t = b`.
nodes.type:
∀ {C : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Categories.Category C] {A B AA T : C}
  {p₁ p₂ : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom AA A} (hP : Foundations.Categories.IsProduct A A AA p₁ p₂)
  (φ : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom AA B),
  (∀ (g : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom A B),
      ∃ a,
        ∀ (x : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom T A),
          Foundations.Categories.Category.comp (hP.lift a x) φ = Foundations.Categories.Category.comp x g) →
    ∀ (t : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom B B), ∃ b, Foundations.Categories.Category.comp b t = b

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.rosser_sep
nodes.doc:
**The Rosser separation lemma.** Let `A(w, x)` and `B(w, x)` be bounded formulas
such that for no `n` both `∃w A(w, n)` and `∃w B(w, n)` hold in `ℕ`. Then `Q` proves
`Sep(n̄)` whenever `∃w A(w, n)` is true, and refutes it whenever `∃w B(w, n)` is true.
nodes.type:
∀ {A B : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith},
  Foundations.Logic.FO.D0 A →
    Foundations.Logic.FO.D0 B →
      (∀ (n w u : Nat), Foundations.Logic.FO.holds A w n → Foundations.Logic.FO.holds B u n → False) →
        ∀ (n : Nat),
          ((∃ w, Foundations.Logic.FO.holds A w n) →
              Foundations.Logic.FO.Q ⊢₁ (Foundations.Logic.FO.sepF A B).inst (Foundations.Logic.FO.numeral n)) ∧
            ((∃ w, Foundations.Logic.FO.holds B w n) →
              Foundations.Logic.FO.Q ⊢₁ ((Foundations.Logic.FO.sepF A B).inst (Foundations.Logic.FO.numeral n)).neg)

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.table_check
nodes.doc:
**The finite verification.** Each of the 24 permutations with `0 ↦ 1` is odd, or its
commutator with the tabulated 3-cycle `g` is the tabulated 3-cycle.
nodes.type:
∀ (k : Fin 24),
  Foundations.Algebra.parity (Foundations.Algebra.Q k) = true ∨
    (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 0 ≠
          Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 1 ∧
        Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 1 ≠
            Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 2 ∧
          Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 0 ≠
            Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 2) ∧
      (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 0 ≠
            Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 1 ∧
          Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 1 ≠
              Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 2 ∧
            Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 0 ≠
              Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 2) ∧
        ∀ (i : Fin 5),
          (Foundations.Algebra.Q k *
                      Foundations.Algebra.c3 (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 0)
                        (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 1)
                        (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 2) *
                    (Foundations.Algebra.Q k)⁻¹ *
                  (Foundations.Algebra.c3 (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 0)
                      (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 1)
                      (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 2))⁻¹).toFun
              i =
            (Foundations.Algebra.c3 (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 0)
                  (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 1)
                  (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 2)).toFun
              i

nodes.doc:
**Dirichlet's sieve applied to the twisted sums.** For `a` coprime to `q`,
`Σ_χ conj χ(a) · S_χ(N) = φ(q) · Σ_{n ≤ N, n ≡ a (q)} Λ(n)/n`.

  a.Coprime q →

        Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal
          (↑(Foundations.Algebra.totient q) *
            Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun n => if n % q = a % q then Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt n / ↑n else 0)
              (N + 1))

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.cabs_gsum_periodic_le
nodes.doc:
**Bounded partial sums.** If `a` is `q`-periodic with `|a(n)| ≤ 1` and `Σ_{n<q} a(n) = 0`,
then `|Σ_{n<N} a(n)| ≤ q` for every `N`.
nodes.type:
∀ {a : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.C} {q : Nat},
  0 < q →
    (∀ (n : Nat), a (n + q) = a n) →
      (∀ (n : Nat), (a n).cabs ≤ 1) →
        Foundations.Numbers.gsum a q = 0 → ∀ (N : Nat), (Foundations.Numbers.gsum a N).cabs ≤ ↑q

nodes.name: Foundations.Sets.WellOrdering.well_ordering_theorem

a strict total order `lt` in which every non-empty part has a least element.
Proved from Zorn's lemma.
nodes.type:
∀ (α : Type u),
  ∃ lt,
    (∀ (x : α), ¬lt x x) ∧
      (∀ (x y z : α), lt x y → lt y z → lt x z) ∧
        (∀ (x y : α), lt x y ∨ x = y ∨ lt y x) ∧ ∀ (S : α → Prop), (∃ x, S x) → ∃ m, S m ∧ ∀ (y : α), S y → ¬lt y m

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.kummer_commute
nodes.doc:
**Kummer radicals.** Let `K ⊆ M` contain a `p`-th root of unity `ζ ≠ 1` (`p` prime), and let
`x ∈ M` with `x^p ∈ K`. Any two automorphisms of `M` fixing `K` commute on `x`: each multiplies
`x` by a power of `ζ`.
nodes.type:
∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω →
    ∀ {p : Nat},
      Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
        ∀ {F M K : Foundations.Algebra.Subfield Ω},
          K.le M →
            ∀ {ζ : Ω},
              ζ ∈ K →
                Foundations.Algebra.rpow ζ p = 1 →
                  ζ ≠ 1 →
                    ∀ (x : { x // x ∈ M }),
                      Foundations.Algebra.rpow x.val p ∈ K →
                        ∀ (a b : Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut F M),
                          a.Fixes K → b.Fixes K → a.toFun (b.toFun x) = b.toFun (a.toFun x)

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.Bisect.spec
nodes.doc:
The bisection invariant: `P` fails at each left end, holds at each right end, the intervals
are ordered, and the `n`-th interval has length `(u − l)/2ⁿ`.
nodes.type:
∀ {P : Foundations.Numbers.Q → Prop} {l u : Foundations.Numbers.Q},
  ¬P l →
    P u →
      l ≤ u →
        ∀ (n : Nat),
          ¬P (Foundations.Numbers.Bisect.lo P l u n) ∧
            P (Foundations.Numbers.Bisect.hi P l u n) ∧
              Foundations.Numbers.Bisect.lo P l u n ≤ Foundations.Numbers.Bisect.hi P l u n ∧
                (Foundations.Numbers.Bisect.hi P l u n - Foundations.Numbers.Bisect.lo P l u n) * 2 ^ n = u - l

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.mul_top
nodes.doc:
**Top coefficients multiply** (list version). If `p` vanishes from index `s + 1` on and
`q` from index `t + 1` on, then the coefficient of `p·q` at `s + t` is `pₛ·qₜ`, and `p·q`
vanishes from index `s + t + 1` on.
nodes.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing R] (q : List R) (t : Nat),
  (∀ (n : Nat), t + 1 ≤ n → Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.coeff q n = 0) →
    ∀ (p : List R) (s : Nat),
      (∀ (n : Nat), s + 1 ≤ n → Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.coeff p n = 0) →
        Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.coeff (Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.mul p q) (s + t) =
            Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.coeff p s * Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.coeff q t ∧
          ∀ (n : Nat), s + t + 1 ≤ n → Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.coeff (Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.mul p q) n = 0

  [inst_4 : Std.LawfulOrderLT F] [inst_5 : Lean.Grind.OrderedRing F] {G : Type} [inst_6 : Lean.Grind.Field G]
  [inst_7 : LE G] [inst_8 : LT G] [inst_9 : Std.IsLinearOrder G] [inst_10 : Std.LawfulOrderLT G]

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.two_qr_iff
nodes.doc:

`p ≡ ±1 (mod 8)`.

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.C.dalembert
nodes.doc:
**d'Alembert's lemma.** If `b₀ ≠ 0`, `b ≠ 0`, `k ≥ 1`, and `r` is bounded on the unit disc,
then `|b₀ + wᵏ (b + w r(w))| < |b₀|` for some `w`: a polynomial does not have a local minimum of
its modulus at a non-zero value.
nodes.type:
∀ {b₀ b : Foundations.Numbers.C},
  b₀ ≠ 0 →
    b ≠ 0 →
      ∀ {k : Nat},
        1 ≤ k →
          ∀ (r : Foundations.Numbers.C → Foundations.Numbers.C) {M : Foundations.Numbers.R},
            (∀ (w : Foundations.Numbers.C), w.cabs ≤ 1 → (r w).cabs ≤ M) →
              ∃ w, (b₀ + w ^ k * (b + w * r w)).cabs < b₀.cabs

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.mle_numM_iff
nodes.doc:
**Everything below a numeral is a numeral.** In a model of `Q`, `x ≤ n̄` (that is,
`d + x = n̄` for some `d`) iff `x = ī` for some `i ≤ n`.
nodes.type:
∀ {M : Foundations.Logic.FO.Structure Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith},
  Foundations.Logic.FO.IsQModel M →
    ∀ (x : M.Dom) (n : Nat),
      Foundations.Logic.FO.mle M x (Foundations.Logic.FO.numM M n) ↔ ∃ i, i ≤ n ∧ x = Foundations.Logic.FO.numM M i

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.lowenheim_skolem
nodes.doc:
**Downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem.** If a theory in a countable language is
satisfied in any structure at all (with domain in `Type`, under some environment),
then it is satisfied in a countable one: a structure admitting a surjection from `ℕ`
onto its domain.
nodes.type:
∀ {L : Foundations.Logic.FO.Signature} [L.Countable] {Γ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Theory L}
  {M : Foundations.Logic.FO.Structure L} {e : Nat → M.Dom},
  (∀ (ψ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula L), Γ ψ → Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat M e ψ) →
    ∃ N e',
      (∀ (ψ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula L), Γ ψ → Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat N e' ψ) ∧
        ∃ f, ∀ (x : N.Dom), ∃ n, f n = x

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.truth_not_ce

**Arithmetical truth is not computably enumerable** (Tarski–Gödel, computational
form): no code halts exactly on the Gödel numbers of the formulas true in `ℕ`.
Otherwise the true non-halting sentences could be enumerated, and the argument above
would apply to this "theory of true arithmetic" in place of PA.
nodes.type:
¬∃ c,
    ∀ (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith),
      Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts c [Foundations.Logic.FO.fcode φ] ↔
        ∀ (e : Nat → Nat), Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel e φ

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.dirichlet_euler
nodes.doc:
**Dirichlet's theorem in Euler's form.** For `q ≥ 1` and `a` coprime to `q`, the sum
`Σ_{p ≤ N, p ≡ a (mod q)} log p / p` is unbounded — the primes in the progression are not only
infinite in number but, weighted by `log p / p`, as plentiful as Mertens' theorem allows
(compare Euler's `Σ 1/p = ∞` for `q = 1`).

∀ {q : Nat},
  0 < q →
    ∀ {a : Nat},
      a.Coprime q →
        ∀ (X : Foundations.Numbers.R),
          ∃ N,
            X ≤
              Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
                (fun p => if Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p ∧ p % q = a % q then (↑p).log / ↑p else 0) (N + 1)

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.PA
nodes.doc:
**The axioms of Peano Arithmetic.** Six closed axioms for successor, addition and
multiplication, plus the induction schema
`φ(0) ∧ ∀x (φ(x) → φ(Sx)) → ∀x φ(x)` for *every* formula `φ` (whose other free
variables act as parameters).

*Remark on the parameters.* The induction instances are kept as *open* formulas, their
parameters being free variables, rather than as universal closures. Since a model of a
theory must satisfy its axioms under every assignment (`IsModel`), and free premises can
be generalised in derivations only through `∀`-introduction with shifted premises, this
is equivalent, for the derivability of sentences, to the textbook formulation with
closed axioms: the closed instances are among our axioms, and conversely the
parameter-free (closed) schema already yields every parametric instance, by applying it
to `ψ(x) := ∀ȳ [φ(0, ȳ) ∧ ∀z (φ(z, ȳ) → φ(Sz, ȳ)) → φ(x, ȳ)]`.

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.homotopy_lifting
nodes.doc:
**Homotopy lifting for the exponential map.** A jointly continuous family `H(s, t)` of points
of the circle (`s, t ∈ [0, 1]`) lifts to a jointly continuous family of angles `L(s, t)`,
`cis L(s, t) = H(s, t)`, starting at any angle `θ₀` over `H(0, 0)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {H : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.C},
  Foundations.Topology.Cont2 H →
    (∀ (s t : Foundations.Numbers.R), 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → (H s t).normSq = 1) →
      ∀ {θ₀ : Foundations.Numbers.R},
        Foundations.Numbers.C.cis θ₀ = H 0 0 →
          ∃ L,
            Foundations.Topology.Cont2 L ∧
              (∀ (s t : Foundations.Numbers.R),
                  0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → Foundations.Numbers.C.cis (L s t) = H s t) ∧
                L 0 0 = θ₀

`a ≤ ⟦φ(x)⟧`.

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Computability.rice
nodes.doc:
**Rice's theorem.** Let `P` be a property of codes that depends only on the
(unary) partial function they compute, and is non-trivial (some code has it, some
does not). Then `P` is undecidable: no code, total on Gödel numbers, outputs `0`
exactly on the numbers of codes lacking `P`.
nodes.type:
∀ (P : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code → Prop),
  (∀ (c c' : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code),
      (∀ (x n : Nat), Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval c [x] n ↔ Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval c' [x] n) →
        (P c ↔ P c')) →
    ∀ {a b : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code},
      P a →
        ¬P b →
          ¬∃ r,
              ∀ (c : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code),
                Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts r [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c] ∧
                  (Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval r [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c] 0 ↔ ¬P c)

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.dsum_prime_pow_mul
nodes.doc:
**Divisor sums over `pᵃ m`** (`p` prime, `p ∤ m`, `m ≥ 1`):

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.mertens_both
nodes.doc:
**Mertens' first theorem, both versions at once.** For `N ≥ 1` the common sum
`S(N) = Σ_{n ≤ N} Λ(n)/n` satisfies the Dirichlet block's bounds `log N − 1 ≤ S(N) ≤ log N + log 1024`
and the PNT block's bounds `−1 ≤ S(N) − log N ≤ log 1024` — which are the same statement.
nodes.type:
∀ {N : Nat},
  1 ≤ N →
    ((↑N).log - 1 ≤ Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun d => Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt d / ↑d) (N + 1) ∧
        Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun d => Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt d / ↑d) (N + 1) ≤
          (↑N).log + Foundations.Numbers.R.log 1024) ∧
      -1 ≤ Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun d => Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt d / ↑d) (N + 1) - (↑N).log ∧
        Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun d => Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt d / ↑d) (N + 1) - (↑N).log ≤
          Foundations.Numbers.R.log 1024

nodes.name: Foundations.Probability.FinProb.E_coord_mul

nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} (P : Foundations.Probability.FinProb α) (X Y : α → Foundations.Numbers.R) {n i j : Nat},
  i < n →
    j < n →
      i ≠ j →
        ((P.pow n).E fun t =>
            Foundations.Probability.FinProb.coord X i t * Foundations.Probability.FinProb.coord Y j t) =
          P.E X * P.E Y

  Foundations.Numbers.R.Vanish e d →

        ∀ (m : Nat) (y : Foundations.Numbers.R),
          Foundations.Numbers.R.poly (Foundations.Numbers.R.iterD m e) d (P - y) =
            (-1) ^ m * Foundations.Numbers.R.poly (Foundations.Numbers.R.iterD m e) d y

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.extend
nodes.doc:
**Extension of embeddings.** Let `σ : F → E` be a ring homomorphism and `δ ∈ E` a root of
`σ(q)` for every `q ∈ F[x]` with `q(γ) = 0`. Then `σ` extends to a ring homomorphism
`τ : F(γ) → E` with `τ(γ) = δ`, given by `τ(p(γ)) = (σ p)(δ)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω] (hΩ : Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω)
  (F : Foundations.Algebra.Subfield Ω) (γ : Ω) (hγ : Foundations.Algebra.IsAlgebraic F γ) {E : Type v}
  [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing E] (σ : Foundations.Algebra.RingHom { x // x ∈ F } E) (δ : E),
  (∀ (q : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial { x // x ∈ F }),
      Foundations.Algebra.aeval F γ q = 0 →
        Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.eval δ (Foundations.Algebra.mapPoly σ q) = 0) →
    ∃ τ,
      (∀ (x : { x // x ∈ F }), τ.toFun ⟨x.val, ⋯⟩ = σ.toFun x) ∧
        τ.toFun ⟨γ, ⋯⟩ = δ ∧
          ∀ (p : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial { x // x ∈ F }),
            τ.toFun ⟨Foundations.Algebra.aeval F γ p, ⋯⟩ =
              Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.eval δ (Foundations.Algebra.mapPoly σ p)

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.sat_induction_of_closed
nodes.doc:
**Parametric induction from parameter-free induction.** If a structure satisfies
the induction axiom of `∀^B indBody φ B` under one environment `e₀`, and `φ` has no
free variables beyond `B`, then it satisfies the induction axiom of `φ` under *every*
environment.
nodes.type:
∀ {M : Foundations.Logic.FO.Structure Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith}
  (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith) (B : Nat),
  (∀ (n : Nat), B ≤ n → Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Fresh n φ) →
    ∀ (e₀ : Nat → M.Dom),
      Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat M e₀
          ((((Foundations.Logic.FO.allN B (Foundations.Logic.FO.indBody φ B)).inst Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith.zero).conj
                ((Foundations.Logic.FO.allN B (Foundations.Logic.FO.indBody φ B)).imp
                    (Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.subst Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith.succSubst
                      (Foundations.Logic.FO.allN B (Foundations.Logic.FO.indBody φ B)))).all).imp
            (Foundations.Logic.FO.allN B (Foundations.Logic.FO.indBody φ B)).all) →
        ∀ (e : Nat → M.Dom),
          Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat M e
            (((φ.inst Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith.zero).conj
                  (φ.imp (Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.subst Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith.succSubst φ)).all).imp
              φ.all)

nodes.doc:
**Reciprocity, classical form.** For distinct odd primes `p`, `q`: if either is `≡ 1 (mod 4)`

  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →

              (p % 4 = 3 ∧ q % 4 = 3 → Foundations.Algebra.legendre p q = -Foundations.Algebra.legendre q p)

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.R.mean_value

`c` strictly between `a` and `b`.
nodes.type:
∀ {f f' : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R} {a b : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  a < b →
    (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), a ≤ x → x ≤ b → Foundations.Numbers.R.ContinuousAt f x) →
      (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), a < x → x < b → Foundations.Numbers.R.HasDerivAt f (f' x) x) →
        ∃ c, a < c ∧ c < b ∧ f b - f a = f' c * (b - a)

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.block_lower
nodes.doc:
**The weight of a block.** If `1 ≤ T`, `2T ≤ m` and `64 T² m² ≤ N`, then the `k` with
`⌊N/(m + ⌊m/T⌋)⌋ < k ≤ ⌊N/m⌋` carry weight `Σ a(k)/k ≥ log N/(8T) − 2 KA`, in the form
`8T · Σ ≥ log N − 16 T KA`.
nodes.type:
∀ {N m T : Nat},
  1 ≤ T →
    2 * T ≤ m →
      64 * (T * T) * (m * m) ≤ N →
        (↑N).log - 16 * ↑T * Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.KA ≤
          8 * ↑T * (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.wsum (N / m) - Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.wsum (N / (m + m / T)))

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.selberg_symmetry_conv
nodes.doc:
**Selberg's symmetry formula, classical form.** For `N ≥ 1`,
`|Σ_{n ≤ N} Λ(n) log n + Σ_{k ≤ N} (Λ ∗ Λ)(k) − 2N log N| ≤ (30 + 4 log 1024) · N`,
i.e. `Σ_{n ≤ x} Λ(n) log n + Σ_{mn ≤ x} Λ(m) Λ(n) = 2x log x + O(x)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {N : Nat},
  1 ≤ N →
    Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs
        (Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum (fun n => Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vonMangoldt n * (↑n).log) (N + 1) +
            Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vmConv (N + 1) -
          2 * ↑N * (↑N).log) ≤
      (30 + 4 * Foundations.Numbers.R.log 1024) * ↑N

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.dominated_convergence
nodes.doc:
**Dominated convergence theorem (Lebesgue).** Let `fₙ` be measurable, `fₙ → f` pointwise, and
`|fₙ| ≤ g` with `g ≥ 0` integrable. Then `f` and all `fₙ` are integrable and
`∫ fₙ dμ → ∫ f dμ`.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} {S : Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.SigmaAlgebra α} (m : Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Measure S)
  {F : Nat → α → Foundations.Numbers.R} {f g : α → Foundations.Numbers.R},
  (∀ (n : Nat), Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Measurable S (F n)) →
    Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.LIntegrable m g →
      (∀ (n : Nat) (x : α), Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (F n x) ≤ g x) →
        (∀ (x : α), Foundations.Numbers.R.Tendsto (fun n => F n x) (f x)) →
          Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Integrable m f ∧
            (∀ (n : Nat), Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Integrable m (F n)) ∧
              Foundations.Numbers.R.Tendsto (fun n => Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.integral m (F n))
                (Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.integral m f)

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.commutator_fixes_step
nodes.doc:
**Commutators fix a radical step.** If `a, b` fix `K` and `x` is a radical step over `K`,
then the commutator `[a, b]` fixes `K` and `x`. (Hence, once we know that automorphisms fixing
`K` and `x` fix `K(x)`, commutators of automorphisms over `K` are automorphisms over `K(x)`:
the abelian character of `Aut(K(x)/K)`.)
nodes.type:
∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω →
    ∀ {K M F : Foundations.Algebra.Subfield Ω} {x : Ω} {p : Nat},
      Foundations.Algebra.KummerStep K x p →
        K.le M →
          ∀ (hx : x ∈ M) (a b : Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut F M),
            a.Fixes K →
              b.Fixes K →
                (Foundations.Algebra.commutator a b).Fixes K ∧
                  (Foundations.Algebra.commutator a b).toFun ⟨x, hx⟩ = ⟨x, hx⟩

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.gsum_mul_gsum

      Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun i => f i * Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun k => g (N - i + k)) i) N

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.residue_sum_le
nodes.doc:
**If the primes `≡ a (mod q)` are all below `N₀`**, then
`Σ_{n ≤ N, n ≡ a} Λ(n)/n ≤ N₀ + 4` for every `N`.
nodes.type:
∀ {q a N₀ : Nat},
  (∀ (p : Nat), Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p → p % q = a % q → p < N₀) →
    ∀ (N : Nat),
      Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun n => if n % q = a % q then Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt n / ↑n else 0)
          (N + 1) ≤
        ↑N₀ + 4

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.legendre_eq_of_pow

nodes.type:
∀ {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    p % 2 = 1 →
      ∀ {a : Nat},
        ¬p ∣ a →
          (a ^ Foundations.Algebra.half p % p = 1 → Foundations.Algebra.legendre a p = 1) ∧
            (a ^ Foundations.Algebra.half p % p = p - 1 → Foundations.Algebra.legendre a p = -1)

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.R.uniform_continuous
nodes.doc:
**Heine–Cantor theorem.** A function continuous at every point of `[a, b]` is *uniformly*
continuous on `[a, b]`: for every `ε > 0` one `δ > 0` works for all pairs of points.
nodes.type:
∀ {f : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R} {a b : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), a ≤ x → x ≤ b → Foundations.Numbers.R.ContinuousAt f x) →
    ∀ {ε : Foundations.Numbers.R},
      0 < ε →
        ∃ δ,
          0 < δ ∧
            ∀ (s t : Foundations.Numbers.R),
              a ≤ s →
                s ≤ b →
                  a ≤ t → t ≤ b → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (s - t) < δ → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (f s - f t) < ε

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.lowenheim_skolem_countable
nodes.doc:
**Löwenheim–Skolem with Part I's countability.** If a theory in a countable
language has a model, it has one whose domain is `Countable` in the sense of

  (∀ (ψ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula L), Γ ψ → Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat M e ψ) →
    ∃ N e',

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.drop_algebra
nodes.doc:
The algebra of the drop: from the block count `J lam ≥ L − c₃` and the weight bound
`J (α − ε/2)(L − 16 T KA) ≤ 8T G`, deduce `G ≥ (ε/(16 T lam)) (L² − (16 T KA + c₃) L)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {ε α L J lam T KA' c₃ G : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  0 < ε →
    ε ≤ α →
      0 < lam →
        0 < T →
          0 ≤ KA' →
            0 ≤ c₃ →
              0 ≤ J →
                16 * T * KA' ≤ L →
                  L - c₃ ≤ J * lam →
                    J * ((α - ε / 2) * (L - 16 * T * KA')) ≤ 8 * T * G →
                      ε / (16 * T * lam) * (L * L - (16 * T * KA' + c₃) * L) ≤ G
